inline.s: [Fertile soil and abundant harvest] The land is fertile and the harvest is good.
[Home and household forever secure] The family is safe and at peace.
[The departed reborn in heaven] Those who have passed on are reborn in heaven to enjoy bliss.
[The living gain longevity] The living gain merit and long life.
[All that is sought is fulfilled] Whatever is sought that is wholesome and reasonable is all brought to satisfaction.
[No flood or fire disasters] Meeting flood or fire, one suffers no harm.
[Waste and loss dispelled] Decline, depletion, and loss are all eliminated. “Waste and loss” means exhausted and emptied.

[Evil dreams cut off] If evil dreams are caused by disharmony of the four elements, one should see a doctor; if they result from karmic hindrances, one should practice the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door and turn evil dreams into auspiciousness.
[Spirits guard one's going and coming] When going out and coming in, ghosts and spirits guard and protect.

[Meeting many causes for sagehood] One meets the causes that transcend the ordinary and enter the sage's state; through practice one gradually cuts off afflictions and will ultimately become a Buddha.
[The ever-present earth spirits] This refers to the ordinary earth spirits.

[If in a future age there are good men and good women who make offerings to the Bodhisattva and recite this sutra, or who practice in a single way according to the Sutra of Ksitigarbha's Original Vows, you shall protect and support them with your original spiritual power.] “One who practices in a single way” has two meanings: first, in practicing the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door one practices at least one method, whether merely prostrating, merely calling the name, or merely reciting the sutra. Second, it comprehensively embraces all the practices of the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door, whether making offerings, reciting, holding in mind, and so on. To those who can study and practice according to this Dharma-door, the Buddha instructed the earth spirits to protect and support them wholeheartedly with their spiritual power.

[Do not let all disasters and adverse matters even reach the ear, much less be experienced] Do not cause this person to be always hearing of all disasters and adverse matters; what he hears is auspicious, and he does not hear even of evil matters, much less experience them personally. The term (rendered here as “zhe”) is pronounced “zhe” and means “always.”

[Naturally and ultimately one escapes the sea of suffering and realizes the bliss of nirvana] In this life one gains the support of sages and virtuous ones as well as of all the heavens, earthly spirits, and gods; in the future one will certainly transcend the sea of suffering of the three realms and realize the bliss of the three-vehicle sage fruits beyond the world. “Good people each have their own heaven”: those who cultivate virtue have an excellent state of their own; even if they meet calamities, they are supported by sages and virtuous ones, and great disasters are reduced to small ones and small ones are reduced to nothing. Practicing the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door, in accord with the Dharma one should obtain such great benefit. But this is only a principle; one must take each person's karmic hindrances into account. It is like a great tree whose seed is small: the tree is large, but the seed is not large because of it. Though the seed is small, after several years of cultivation its foliage becomes luxuriant enough to provide shade. But if it is planted in sand, soil, or broken tiles, where nourishment is insufficient, its growth will be affected. Cultivation is likewise: do not be disappointed because you have not gained the great benefit the sutra describes; rather, you should examine yourself: how is the merit of your practice? Is it earnest and reverent? If one receives and holds it with a sincere mind and yet gains little benefit, it is because the karma of past lives was heavy; it may be that a heavy retribution is being received lightly. Cause and effect are complex; you should deeply believe the Buddha's words and give rise to no doubt!

blocks.text: Chapter Twelve: The Benefits of Seeing and Hearing

inline.s: The Buddha emitted light from the crown of his head and, with a wonderful voice, praised and extolled Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva asked about the inconceivable matters, and the Buddha answered them severally.
[The crown gate] In ancient China it was held that the human head is like a hall, and the whorl at the crown is called the heavenly gate; hence it is called the crown gate.
[The hair-mark radiance] A metaphor for the hundreds of thousands and millions of kinds of light emitted by the Buddha, pure, clear, and translucent.
[The great hair-mark] It represents the vast and supreme radiance that universally illuminates the ten directions.
[The auspicious hair-mark] The light reveals all manner of auspicious signs.

[The jade hair-mark] The earth-crystal is called jade; touched, it is cool and refreshing, and its light and color are pure. Sentient beings receiving it have their heat and affliction suddenly stilled, and body and mind become cool and clear.
[The purple hair-mark] A color mingling black and red.
[The blue hair-mark] A blue light.
[The azure hair-mark] A deep blue light.
[The green hair-mark] A leaf-green light.
[The auspicious clouds] The light is like clouds, revealing an auspicious appearance.
[The thousand wheels] Within the light appear a thousand kinds of wheel-marks.
[The jewel wheel] The light manifests wheel-marks, with colors jewel-like and splendid.
[The sun wheel] The light is like a wheel, surpassing the sun.
[The moon wheel] The light is like the moon, round and cool and clear.
[The palaces] Within the light appear palaces, solemn and surpassingly excellent.

[The ocean-cloud] The light is layer upon layer without end, like clouds emerging from a mountain peak (the character here is read “xiu”, the peak of a mountain or mountain range), vast and boundless, pervading the ten directions — this is what is called the “incense-cloud canopy.”

[Listen now, today, in the Trayastrimsa palace, as I praise and extol Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva — the matters of his benefiting humans and gods, the inconceivable matters, the matters of transcending the cause of sagehood, the matters of realizing the ten stages, and the matter of ultimately never retreating from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.] These are the words of the World-Honored One praising Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. The Buddha instructed the assembly and all beings: listen now, today, in the Trayastrimsa heaven, as I praise and extol Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva — the matters of his benefiting humans and gods, the matters of his inconceivable spiritual powers, wisdom, and skillful means; the matters of practicing according to this Dharma-door so as to transcend the ordinary and enter the sage's state, to advance from the position of an ordinary person into the three worthy positions of the ten faiths, the ten abodes, and the ten practices, and even to realize the position of the ten stages, walking the bodhisattva's path; and, being transformed by the Great Being Ksitigarbha, the matter of ultimately becoming a Buddha.
[Just now] A moment ago.

[You have a great karmic connection with the Saha world. Whether gods or dragons, whether men or women, whether spirits or ghosts — even the suffering beings of the six paths — those who hear your name, see your form, long for you, or praise you: these beings, in the unsurpassed Way, will surely never retreat; they will always be reborn among humans, fully enjoying wonderful bliss, and when their causes and fruits are ripe, they will meet the Buddha and receive the prophecy.] The Buddha praises Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva's supreme virtue as being the same as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's. If sentient beings of the six paths practice the Avalokitesvara Dharma-door — hearing the name, seeing the form, praising, longing for, admiring, and esteeming the virtue — they will surely never retreat from the unsurpassed fruit of Buddhahood. Before becoming Buddhas, they fully enjoy the wonderful bliss of humans and gods; when their wholesome causes and fruits are ripe, they meet the Buddha and receive the prophecy that they will certainly become Buddhas in the future. This shows the deep karmic connection between Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva and sentient beings.

[When the heavenly blessings are exhausted] The lifespan of heavenly beings is very long; yet, long though it is, when their blessings are exhausted they fall again — either to the human world or to the three evil paths — as determined by the ripening of their karmic causes. Heavenly beings have no signs of aging; when the signs of decline appear, they know they will die.

[The five signs of decline] When heavenly beings are about to die, five signs of decline appear before them: first, the flowers on the head wither — the flower crown worn on the head gradually withers; second, the garments become soiled and greasy — the seamless heavenly robes give rise to stains; third, the body becomes foul — not only does the light of the heavenly body disappear, but also a great deal of foul odor flows out; fourth, sweat under the armpits — great quantities of foul sweat flow from beneath the two armpits; fifth, dissatisfaction with one's own seat — after these various bad signs of decline appear, the heavenly being becomes discontented with his own precious seat, and his heavenly consorts and attendants, being repelled, leave him. When the Buddha was in the world, a heavenly being's five signs of decline appeared; perceiving that he would fall into the animal path as a pig and seeing the defiled life of pigs, he sought help from the lord of the Trayastrimsa heaven. The lord led him to see the Buddha, and the Buddha taught him to bring forth the resolve to take refuge. At once, through the merit of taking refuge in the Three Jewels, the signs of decline were reversed and his heavenly blessings increased. Even taking refuge yields such a reward — how much more so for further practicing the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door.
[Necklace] An ornament strung with pearls and jade and worn around the neck.
[Sincere refuge] To call the name and bow with utmost sincerity is sufficient.

[And further, may Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, endowed with great compassion, forever protect me; then in sleep and in dreams this person will receive the Bodhisattva's touching the crown of the head and the prophecy.] If good, faithful men and women seek Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva — endowed with great compassion, protecting and blessing me to the end of the future — and, practicing in accord with the teaching, are moved by their utmost sincerity, then in dreams they will receive the Bodhisattva's prophecy of becoming a Buddha.
[Playthings] Objects that can be displayed and admired; here they refer to things for adorning the Buddha hall and the Ksitigarbha hall, not children's toys.

[Turning to face the south, and as it is about to enter the mouth, with utmost sincerity and reverence.] When drinking, face the south to signify that the Great Being comes from the south. But it is not necessarily required to face directly south; one may turn sideways, so as not to face or turn one's back to the Great Being, as a sign of respect. As the water is about to enter the mouth, silently invoke the holy name in the mind with utmost sincerity and earnestness, seeking the compassionate aid of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.
[The five pungent plants] Also called the five strong-smelling vegetables: the five pungent vegetables. These five are: garlic, scallion, small garlic, chives, and asafoetida.
[Bestowing the water of consecration] Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva pours the nectar-water upon the head of the practitioner.
[What is sought is thwarted] What is sought cannot be fulfilled as wished.

[Therefore, O Avalokitesvara! Do you spread this sutra through your spiritual power, so that the sentient beings of the Saha world may forever enjoy peace and bliss for hundreds of thousands and millions of kalpas.] The Buddha instructed Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva to spread this sutra through spiritual power, so that sentient beings, practicing in accord with the Dharma, may eliminate disasters and increase blessings, have their karmic hindrances melted away like ice, and their path-endeavors grow, and in the future surely attain bodhi.

[If a person hears the name of Ksitigarbha, or even sees the image and bows in reverence; with incense, flowers, clothing, and food he makes offerings — offering to hundreds and thousands, he enjoys wonderful bliss. If he can dedicate this to the dharma-realm, he will ultimately become a Buddha and transcend birth and death.] If sentient beings hear the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, see the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and joyfully make offerings, even if they have not yet gained liberation, they can be reborn in the heavens or among humans and enjoy supremely wonderful bliss. If they can dedicate this merit to the dharma-realm, they will certainly become a Buddha in the future; before becoming a Buddha, practicing in accord with the teaching and receiving it with faith, without retreating from the mind of the Way, they can transcend the suffering of birth and death in the three realms, and further turn from the lesser to the greater, bring forth the bodhi-mind, and continue until they become Buddhas.

blocks.text: Chapter Thirteen: The Entrustment to Humans and Gods

inline.s: The Buddha again caressed the crown of Ksitigarbha's head and entrusted to him all beings to be delivered. Next, for Akasagarbha Bodhisattva, he spoke of the twenty-eight kinds of benefit for people in the world who see the image, hear the sutra, recite the sutra, bow, and pay homage; and again he spoke of the seven kinds of benefit for gods, dragons, ghosts, and spirits who hear the name, bow, and pay homage.

[Entrustment] “Entrust” means to entrust; “lei” has the sense of trouble, burden, or being put to the trouble. The Buddha once more entrusted the beings of humans and gods to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to bear the responsibility.

[The beings of the southern Jambudvipa are of unstable aspiration and nature; many cultivate evil.] The beings of this Jambudvipa lack steadfast will in practice, have strong evil habits, and readily create evil karma.
[Gradually cultivate the unsurpassed] Lead them gradually toward the path of bodhi.

[How much more so for those who, hearing all virtuous matters, practice in thought after thought — they will naturally never retreat from the unsurpassed Way.] How much more so for those who, hearing all virtuous matters, practice in thought after thought within the Buddha-Dharma: I will surely strive to protect and support them, to uproot the fundamental suffering of birth and death, and on the Buddha's path they will never retreat.

Having seen and heard such scripture and known the vast and deep compassionate vow of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, let sentient beings bring forth a constant mind, with a fixed daily practice — holding and reciting, bowing, cultivating contemplation, and so on. As long as one accomplishes “commit no evil, practice all good, and purify one's own mind,” one will surely receive aid and protection, and the path-endeavor will be accomplished. Even a single thought is protected; how much more so for one who practices in thought after thought! Those who study Buddhism, hearing this, should strengthen their mind of the Way and resolve never to waver. Though now their hindrances are heavy and they are born in the Latter Dharma, they still have the good fortune to draw near the Three Jewels. Do not retreat because of small adversities; do not disappoint the compassionate mind and compassionate vows of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
[Akasagarbha Bodhisattva] One of the eight great Bodhisattvas. Because this Bodhisattva stores up all merit like space itself, he is named Akasagarbha.

[If in a future age there are good men and good women who see the image of Ksitigarbha and hear this sutra, even to reciting it, and with incense, flowers, food and drink, clothing, and precious jewels make offerings, and praise and gaze in reverence, they obtain twenty-eight kinds of benefit.] If in a future age there are good men and women who hear the meaning of this sutra and recite or chant it, see the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, make offerings of incense, flowers, food and drink, clothing, and precious jewels, and praise and gaze in reverence — whichever method of practice, all obtain the twenty-eight kinds of benefit.
Recitation and chanting are themselves praise, because the scripture often praises the Great Being. If one specifically holds the name, one should first offer praise.
[Protected and remembered by gods and dragons] The eight classes of gods and dragons respectfully protect.
[Good fruits increase day by day] Practicing the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door, wholesome causes increase and good fruits are accomplished.
[Gathering the supreme cause of sagehood] Increase and accumulate the cause of unsurpassed bodhi, and be able to transcend the ordinary and enter the sage's state.
[No retreat from bodhi] In the unsurpassed Way, diligently progress without slackening.
[Suffcient clothing and food] Before becoming a Buddha, enjoyments are without lack; unless karma is heavy, it is not easily changed.
[Pestilence does not come] One does not suffer the affliction of disease and plague.
[Apart from flood and fire disasters] Through regular practice, one can eliminate natural disasters such as flood and fire.
[No calamities of robbers and thieves] Far from the dangers and harms of robbers and thieves.
[People who see you admire and respect] People who see you are delighted and respect and admire you.
[Spirits and ghosts aid and hold] The underworld ghosts and spirits, even those who were evil, turn to good and help and protect.
[A woman turns to a man's body] The sixth chapter has said: if a woman is weary of the female body and practices this Dharma-door, in the future she will turn from woman to man.

[A daughter of kings and ministers] If one is not weary of the female body, then in hundreds of thousands and millions of billions of lives one will always be a king's daughter, even a king's consort, or of the great families of ministers and high officials, or the daughter of a great elder.
[Upright and well-featured] Reborn upright and dignified, with all the marks complete.

[Often reborn in the heavens] If one has no other aspiration, one is often reborn in the heavens; because of the Great Being's vow to keep sentient beings from falling into evil paths and to deliver them at the three assemblies of the dragon-flower in the future, if one does not seek rebirth in a Buddha-land, the cause is mostly rebirth in the heavens.
[Or become an emperor] Life after life born among humans, a king of people.
[Past wisdom and the superknowledges] Life after life endowed with wisdom, possessing the power of recalling past lives, able to continue one's practice and quickly attain accomplishment.
[All that is sought is granted] Reasonable and wholesome requests are all brought to satisfaction.
[Family and relatives rejoicing] The family is harmonious and happy.
[All untoward calamities destroyed] Practicing the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door, in principle one does not meet with sudden calamities.

[The paths of karma forever removed] Letting go of the butcher's knife, one becomes a Buddha on the spot. One can remove the contributory conditions for creating evil karma and forever escape the suffering of the three evil paths.
[Everywhere one goes, all is open] In going, coming, and moving about, everything is free and unobstructed, and affairs go smoothly.

[Peaceful dreams at night] Before sleeping, silently invoke the holy name, and at night there will be no evil dreams. Evil dreams are the karmic effects of past lives; practicing the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door can dissolve karmic hindrances, and so the night-dreams are peaceful and happy.
[The departed depart from suffering] Through dedicating the merit, one's deceased parents and ancestors depart from suffering and attain bliss.
[Reborn through past blessings] Practicing the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door, one enjoys great blessings through successive lives.
[Praised by the sages] The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas rejoice, praise, and aid.
[Intelligent and of keen faculties] As the twelfth chapter says: the scripture that passes through the ear is never forgotten, because wisdom has opened.

[An abundant heart of compassion] The Great Being's compassionate heart is supreme; transforming and guiding the beings in hell, the practitioner, moved by the Great Being, “thinks of the sufferings of hell and brings forth the bodhi-mind.” The compassionate heart grows, pitying the suffering of sentient beings. “Abundant” means full and rich.
[Ultimate Buddhahood] The ultimate and complete realization of the fruit of Buddhahood. This is the thoroughgoing goal of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's deliverance of beings.
[Swiftly transcending to the sage's ground] Swiftly transcend the ordinary realm and enter the sage's position.
[Evil karma destroyed] Wholesome karma increases and flourishes, and evil karma is eliminated.
[Protected by all Buddhas] The Buddhas of the ten directions constantly protect and remember.
[No retreat from bodhi] On the path to Buddhahood, one does not retreat.
[Increasing original powers] Gods, dragons, ghosts, and spirits originally have minor spiritual powers; practicing the Ksitigarbha Dharma-door, they can increase their spiritual powers and might.
[The recollection of past lives all open] The power of recalling past lives increases and excels, knowing the affairs of many past lives.
[Rain] To fall.

blocks.text: Notes on Reciting the Sutra of the Original Vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

inline.s: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, by his incomparable power of vow — “Only when all beings have been delivered will I realize bodhi; as long as hell is not empty, I vow not to become a Buddha” — delivers us, the suffering beings. Reciting the Sutra of the Original Vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva not only eliminates disasters and averts difficulties, resolves grievances and loosens knots, and makes all that is done auspicious, but also yields countless inconceivable merits and benefits. (See the scripture for details.)
1. Prayer before reciting (palms together):
Namo to the great-vow, great-power, compassionate and merciful King Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva (recite three times)
I pray that the Bodhisattva will bless and protect this disciple
as he recites the Sutra of the Original Vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.
2. During the recitation:
One should read aloud, but there is no need for a loud voice. The key is to recite with a sincere, reverent, and repentant mind; read clearly, and, as much as possible, hear clearly.
3. Dedication after reciting (palms together):
I, this disciple
, wish to dedicate the merit of reciting the Sutra of the Original Vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to this disciple's

karmic creditors and wronged ones from life after life. I pray that the great-vow, great-power, compassionate and merciful King Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will, in his compassion, act as refuge and deliver them, so that karmic hindrances are eliminated, they depart from suffering and attain bliss, and are reborn in the Pure Land. I, this disciple
, sincerely repent. (Speak aloud sincerely, three times.)
Then recite the dedication verse:
May I be born in the Western Pure Land, with the nine grades of lotus blossom as my parents
May the blossom open, seeing the Buddha and awakening to non-arising, with non-retreating bodhisattvas as companions

(Note: this dedication is to be made to one's own karmic creditors and wronged ones from life after life. Because they are closely related to you and most readily entangle and obstruct you, you should first deliver them. After resolving their problems, you may then bring forth the resolve to dedicate the merit to all beings in the dharma-realm and seek rebirth in the Pure Land.)

blocks.text: A Table of Difficult Characters in the Mantra

inline.s: Om (read weng), Li (read li), He (read he), Fu (read wa), Luo (read la), Da (read da), Hu (read hong), Duo (read duo), Namo (read na-mo, meaning taking refuge), Tuo (read tuo), Nan (read nan), Wei (read wei), O (read ye), Nang (read nang), Wa (read wa), Shu (read shu), Han (read han), Pi (read pi), Qie (read qie), Qian (read qian), Na (read nuo), Qu (read qie), Nu (read nu), Lu (read lu), Suo (read suo)
